title: Subsets
prompt:
Given an array of **unique** integers, return all possible subsets (the power set), in any order, with no duplicate subsets.

**Example**: `[1,2,3]` → `[[],[1],[2],[1,2],[3],[1,3],[2,3],[1,2,3]]`.

**Constraints**: 1 ≤ n ≤ 10.
hints: Each element is either in a subset or not. How can you build subsets one choice at a time without producing both [1,2] and [2,1]?
Backtrack with a `start` index: record the current `path` at every call, then for `i` from `start`, add `nums[i]`, recurse with `i + 1`, and remove it.
Record with `res.add(new ArrayList<>(path))`. If you add `path` itself, every entry points at the same list, which ends up empty.

solution.explanation: Every call in the recursion tree corresponds to exactly one subset, so recording at every call collects them all. `start` keeps indices increasing, so each subset is built only once. 2ⁿ subsets, each copied in O(n): O(n·2ⁿ) time, O(n) recursion depth.
